newsitem.title: TURKEY: Former Turkish top policeman arrested in scandal.
newsitem.headline: Former Turkish top policeman arrested in scandal.

text.p: Turkey's former deputy head of police intelligence was arrested on Wednesday in an eavesdropping scandal that has set the powerful military at odds with the former Islamist-led government.
Anatolian news agency said policeman Bulent Orakoglu was detained after a military court had charged him with "taking documents and information relating to state security".

Orakoglu is accused of running a mole within the secularist armed forces and passing on information and documents about army monitoring of Islamists to the government of former prime minister Necmettin Erbakan.
Orakoglu faces a maximum of 10 years in prison.
Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamit leader, resigned in June after months of back-stage pressure from the secularist military.

The army on Tuesday demanded the prosecution of former interior minister Meral Aksener for allegedly insulting the armed forces in a news conference she gave last week in which she acknowledged police had spied on the military.
